sweatbox.title: SweatBox Scenario Generator
sweatbox.description: Write EuroScope simulator scenarios by seat. Tick the positions being trained, set the traffic level, and the stands, runways and coordinates come straight from the sector packages — no degrees, minutes and seconds typed by hand.
sweatbox.copyFailed: Copy failed — select it from the preview instead
sweatbox.loadFailed: Could not load that airport. Try again.

TWR.name: TWR — Tower
TWR.hint: Arrivals on final, spaced down the glide

APP.name: APP — Approach
APP.hint: Arrivals only: inbound at level, outside in

setup.title: Field and seats
setup.subtitle: Where, which position, and how much traffic
setup.elevationHint: Written as AIRPORT_ALT, which is what puts the ground where it belongs; parked aircraft themselves are written at 0
setup.arrivalRunwayHint: TWR and APP arrivals are placed against it
setup.departureRunwayHint: DEP traffic climbs out along its upwind
setup.profilesHint: Multi-select. Each one adds its own traffic — tick GND alone and nothing is airborne.
setup.trafficHint: The three levels are shortcuts; every count below is yours to set.
setup.ilsHint: Selected runways get an ILS line — threshold plus far end, so magnetic variation cannot skew it
setup.controllersHint: Filled in from the airport and the ticked seats, and left alone once you edit it
setup.initialSeatHint: Written as INITIALPSEUDOPILOT on every aircraft. Sign in as this position and the whole scenario is yours without taking each aircraft by hand. Blank leaves them on PSEUDOPILOT:ALL.
setup.routesHint: Referenced by an aircraft's $ROUTE, e.g. a departure track
setup.spacingHint: Minutes between consecutive aircraft. Written as a START schedule; equal values give a metronome.

header.title: Scenario header
header.subtitle: The global settings at the head of the file

aircraft.title: Aircraft
aircraft.pickAirportHint: Stands, runways and fixes are loaded per airport from the sector packages.
aircraft.emptyHint: Pick the seats and the traffic level, then generate — or add them one at a time per seat.
aircraft.heading: Heading

preview.title: Output
preview.problems: These load without complaint and then behave oddly
preview.hint: Save as .txt in EuroScope's SweatBox scenario directory. Line endings are CRLF, matching the existing scenarios.

problems.type: {count} aircraft use a type with no performance block and will fall back to the generic model
problems.elevation: No field elevation — parked aircraft would be written at 0 ft
problems.stands: Not enough stands — GND asks for {count} more than the field has

sources.title: Traffic sources
sources.description: Callsigns, types and the other end of each flight rotate through these pools.
sources.typesHint: Comma separated; only types with a performance block
sources.partnersHint: Where departures go and arrivals came from
sources.radialsHint: Comma-separated bearings to spread APP arrivals across; blank puts them all on the landing runway's reciprocal
sources.seedHint: The same seed gives the same scenario, so a session can be re-run verbatim
sources.equipmentHint: Rides after the type as B738/L — the same shape a member files
sources.cruiseHint: Blank picks the Chinese semicircular level from each leg s track and length; fill it to pin every strip to one level
sources.routeNote: Routes are planned over the airway network: departures pick up airways at the SID exit, arrivals end on the STAR and landing runway

errors.title: Planted mistakes
errors.hint: Give a share of the plans something wrong for the trainee to catch on clearance. The hand-written sets do the same and keep the answers in a separate note.
errors.keyHint: Shown here only — never written into the scenario file.

portal.title: Instructors & Management
portal.description: The network's management side: train students, approve promotions, run events, stock prizes, publish case outcomes. Which cards you see depends on your rating.

aipAccess.title: Aeronautical database access
aipAccess.description: Who may open database.ceruleanavi.net. Only an ADM can change it, and it is separate from controlling rating — someone who proofreads charts may hold no rating, and holding one does not mean editing procedure coding.

grant.title: Grant access
grant.help: Search by CAN ID or name. Read browses everything; write also edits — editing is not built yet, but the level can be issued now.

current.title: Current holders
current.emptyHelp: Search for a member above to grant it.

servers.title: Server directory
servers.description: Clients ask this for the FSD, voice and datafeed addresses instead of compiling them in. Edit a row here and the next server move costs no desktop releases.
servers.emptyHelp: Add one above. While it is empty, clients fall back to their own compiled-in addresses.

add.title: Add a server
add.help: The kind decides what to fill in: FSD and voice want a host and port, a datafeed wants a full URL. Lower sort keys come first; clients treat the first as the default.
